title: Cluenite — Twitch demo and build story

segments.title: What is Cluenite?
lines: What if chat could solve a mystery while you take a break?
This is Cluenite: a Twitch-native mystery game for streamers and their communities.
segments.proof: Actual Quick Case overlay in the stream context. No 3D intro. Existing OBS stills are dated evidence, not a continuous take.

segments.title: Chat discovers the first clue
lines: Viewers play in ordinary Twitch chat. In Quick Case, someone inspects the camera with the look command.
The message reaches EventSub, and the overlay releases a clue: tag R zero seven.
The streamer keeps their main scene; chat now has something to investigate.
segments.proof: Record !look CAM in an owner-controlled Twitch channel and the corresponding Q01 CAM_R07 evidence appearing.

segments.title: Connect evidence and earn the verdict
lines: Inspect the maintenance schedule, then connect the records. The same robot was scheduled in that gallery at twenty-one ten.
The engine checks the proof before revealing the answer. Every useful observation can move the case forward.
segments.proof: Record !look SCHEDULE, !link CAM_R07 SCHEDULE_R07 and !solve ROBOT; hold the actual Q01 reveal.

segments.title: Dashboard and Mystery Live
lines: Quick Case is the short format. Mystery Live gives the community a longer investigation.
Inspect the scene, build an evidence board, reconstruct the timeline, and challenge a theory.
Here, the festival trophy disappears around a blackout. The obvious explanation is theft. But what happened before the lights went out?
segments.proof: Record the actual host dashboard and a new server-backed M01 session. A public visual preview cannot stand in for that session.

segments.title: A wrong theory becomes the next lead
lines: Putting the blackout first does not fit the records.
The heat warning, safety order, opened display and departing trolley all come earlier.
Correct the order, then challenge the theft theory: the authorized move began before the blackout.
A theory is tested against evidence, so a wrong guess becomes the next lead.
segments.proof: Record M01's wrong order, accepted HEAT ORDER OPEN TROLLEY BLACKOUT, and the BLACKOUT_THEFT / ACCESS_RECORD contradiction.

segments.title: Two communities, one breakthrough
lines: Co-op gives two communities different workstations in the same investigation.
The field station scans the signal. The records station checks the maintenance manual.
Share both discoveries and the server unlocks a joint proof. Neither community starts with the whole answer.
Each side contributes something the other needs, turning a deduction into a shared breakthrough.
segments.proof: Use a fresh real-provider C01 UI take. Backend acceptance reports alone do not provide moving gameplay footage.
fallbackLines: Cluenite is also designed around the streamer's workflow.
The guide explains chat commands. Settings keep presentation preferences together, and setup explains how to add the browser overlay.
These are the actual local pages at desktop and phone widths.
A short mystery can fit around the main broadcast, while Mystery Live gives a community room for a longer investigation.
segments.fallbackProof: The original script's 32-second fallback: existing signed-out responsive recordings. Clearly label local interface / 390 and 1280 px. Do not narrate the co-op version over this footage.

segments.title: How Cluenite was built with Codex
lines: We built Cluenite with OpenAI Codex, starting from case rules.
Codex helped implement the engine, EventSub, persistent sessions and realtime updates.
Automated tests and real Twitch-to-OBS runs checked the logic.
The server verifies evidence; the overlay presents the result.
segments.proof: Actual repository source and dated build handoff; fresh engine test result; real Twitch-to-OBS evidence. Do not create a fake Codex chat or session ID.

segments.title: Close on the actual result
lines: One clue can change the whole story.
Cluenite turns downtime into a mystery and chat into investigators.
Built for streamers. Solved together.
segments.proof: Return to the recorded Q01 reveal. Only show repository/channel links that the owner has approved and judges can open.
